summary: Defines the MIME types associated with MP4 files and recommends which registered type to use depending on the kind of content. This helps servers and mail programs label audio and video files correctly. It is standards-track and was later updated by RFC 6381.

eli5.summary: Every file needs a label on the outside so computers know if it is music or a movie. This sets the labels for MP4 files.

questions: which media type should mp4 audio use
subtitle: Which MIME type to put on an MP4 file, depending on whether it holds video, audio or neither.

tldr.problem: MP4 files can hold very different kinds of MPEG-4 content, and servers and mail programs need a standard label to attach when they serve them, for example over HTTP.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers five MIME types with IANA and gives simple rules for choosing among them: video/mp4 for most files, audio/mp4 for audio-only files and application/mp4 for files with neither audio nor video.
tldr.outcome: Servers have a standard type to use for MP4 files. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and was later updated by RFC 6381.

today: RFC 4337 is a Proposed Standard and was later updated by RFC 6381. Read the two together when you need the current picture.

sections.title: Why MP4 Needs MIME Types
sections.content:
RFC 4337 defines the standard MIME types for MP4 files and gives guidelines for using them. A MIME type is the label a server or mail program attaches to a file so the receiver knows what kind of data it is.

The RFC says the MP4 file type is used as an interchange format for ISO/IEC 14496 data, as a content-download format and as the format read by streaming media servers. The first two uses are easier if there is one standard MIME type for serving these files, for example over HTTP.
sections.eli5: A file has no face, so the computer reads its label to know what it is. This RFC makes sure everyone uses the same label for MP4 files.

sections.title: MPEG-4 and the MP4 File Type
sections.content:
MPEG-4 (ISO/IEC 14496) is a standard for representing and delivering multimedia over many transport protocols. It covers interactive scene management, visual and audio representations, and system functions such as multiplexing, synchronization and an object descriptor framework.

Amendment 1 of the standard (also called version 2) introduced a file type for packaging this data, called the MP4 file. It is specified separately as the MP4 file format, which is based on the ISO base media file format. A further specification covers storing Advanced Video Coding (AVC, also known as H.264) in files of that kind.

What is inside an MP4 file varies a lot: compressed video and audio, interactive scene information, metadata, or references to MPEG-4 streams outside the file. The RFC notes that the historical approach for MPEG data has been to declare it under video, with some types under audio and application for streams without a visual presentation.
sections.eli5: An MP4 is like a lunch box that can hold a movie, a song or just notes. Because the contents differ, the label on the box needs to differ too.

sections.title: Choosing the Right Type
sections.content:
The type is picked according to what the file contains. The RFC gives three basic guidelines:

  • If the file has neither visual nor audio presentation, only things such as MPEG-J or MPEG-7, use application/mp4.
  • For all other files, including those that have MPEG-J and similar content in addition to video or audio streams, video/mp4 should be used.
  • For files with audio but no visual aspect, including those with MPEG-J and similar content alongside the audio, audio/mp4 may be used.

In every case the type indicates a file conforming to the MP4 specification, the ISO/IEC 14496-1:2000 systems file format. Note the wording: video/mp4 is a SHOULD for most files, while audio/mp4 is only a MAY for audio-only files.
sections.eli5: If the box holds a movie, call it a movie. If it holds only music, you may call it music. If it holds neither, call it a plain data file.

sections.title: The Five Registered Types
sections.content:
The IANA section registers five new MIME types. Each has the same registration details: no required or optional parameters, intended usage Common, application area Multimedia, no magic number, file extensions mp4 and mpg4, and the Macintosh file type code mpg4. The contact and change controller is David Singer, the ISO/IEC 14496 file format chair.

  • video/mp4: an MP4 file.
  • audio/mp4: an MP4 file with audio but without visual presentation.
  • application/mp4: an MP4 file with an MPEG-4 system stream and neither visual nor audio presentation.
  • application/mpeg4-iod: an Initial Object Descriptor in binary format.
  • application/mpeg4-iod-xmt: an Initial Object Descriptor in textual format.

For the binary types the encoding consideration is that base64 is generally preferred, because the files are binary and should be transmitted without CR/LF conversion or 7-bit stripping. For the textual IOD type, the encoding consideration is listed as none.
sections.eli5: Five new labels are added to the official label list: one for movies, one for music, one for other MP4 data, and two for a small description card that goes with MPEG-4 content.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The main risk is that someone injects non-compliant MPEG streams (audio, video or systems) into an MP4 file to overload the receiver's or decoder's buffers. That could compromise the receiver or even crash it, especially in end-to-end systems like MPEG where buffer models are precisely defined.

An MP4 file can also store commands that the terminal executes, such as OD and BIFS commands, and programmatic content such as MPEG-J (Java byte code) and ECMAScript. Used in a non-compliant way, these could crash the receiver or make it temporarily unavailable.

The RFC says authentication mechanisms can validate the sender and the data. It also notes that ISO/IEC 14496 defines a security model for MPEG-J: downloaded byte code is forbidden to load libraries, define native methods, start programs, read or write files, or read system properties.
sections.eli5: A sneaky person could pack a file with tricks that make a player choke or crash. The rules say to check who sent the file, and the built-in programs in it are not allowed to touch the rest of your computer.
